description.narrative: The most significant expected project-level outcomes are the generation of foreign exchange revenue for Tanzania, increased local value addition, and employment. IFC estimates that the Project will generate indirect and induced jobs along the different value chains as the supply and logistics networks are expected to grow significantly due to the expansion. Beyond the Project, IFC expects the investment to continue strengthening the integration of manufacturing industries on a regional scale, by further optimizing regional supply chains of glass packaging, which could serve as catalysts for developing additional downstream linkages, for instance, with the emerging beverage, food, pharmaceutical, perfume and cosmetics industries in Eastern and Southern Africa.

The proposed investment is a debt facility to Kioo Limited (Kioo or the Company), a leading glass container producer in East Africa. Kioo produces both flint and colored glass for its domestic market in Tanzania, where it has dominant market share, and export markets in Eastern, Central, and Southern Africa, and the Indian Ocean Islands. Its customers include leading beverage multinationals. The project will support the planned capacity expansion of Kioo in its existing production facility in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania (the Project). The expansion will enable the Company to meet increasing demand for glass containers in the region. The key components of the Project are addition of a new production line and addition of transportation equipment.
